sources.name: eesel AI: Captions AI features, pricing and limitations

caption:
Captions turns a talking video into an edited, captioned clip from your phone.
The free plan has no AI credits, and AI features need a paid plan to export.
Here is how AI Edit, captions and dubbing work, and what each plan gets you.

Would you let an AI edit your videos for you?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Captions Help Center · Photo: Captions
threads_text: Captions can cut, caption and even dub your talking videos with AI. The catch: the free plan has no AI credits, and paid plans start at $24.99 a month for 500 credits. Would you pay for an AI video editor?

slides.headline: How to use *Captions AI*: edit, caption and dub your videos from your phone

slides.heading: 1. Start an *AI Edit*
paras: On Home, keep Edit selected, add your clip, pick a style and tap Continue.
Choose an effort level from Quick to Ultra, then tap Create project.

slides.heading: 2. Fix your *eye contact*
paras: The Eye Contact tool in the editing panel corrects your gaze after you record.
Exporting a project that uses it needs a paid plan.

slides.heading: 3. Dub it into *another language*
paras: Dubbing covers 30+ languages. Lipdub also moves your lips to match.

paras.t: Dubbing is capped at 5 minutes per video.

slides.heading: 4. Know the *credits*
paras: Free has no AI credits. Max is $24.99 a month for 500 credits.
You see a credit estimate before each AI Edit, and unused credits roll over.

slides.hook: Follow for AI tool guides that tell you the limits before you pay.

site_article.headline: How to use Captions AI: AI Edit, captions, dubbing and plans explained
site_article.dek: Captions edits talking videos for you on iPhone, Android and the web. Here is how AI Edit, captions and dubbing work, and what the credits and plans really cost.
site_article.summary: Captions is an AI video editor from Mirage that cuts, captions, translates and dubs talking videos. The free plan includes basic editing but no AI credits, and paid plans start at $24.99 a month for 500 credits.
site_article.seo_title: How to use Captions AI: AI Edit, captions and plans
site_article.seo_description: How to use Captions AI step by step: run AI Edit, add captions in about 100 languages, dub videos, export, and see what the free and paid plans include.
site_article.answer_summary: Open the Captions app, keep Edit selected on Home, add your clip, pick a style and an effort level, and tap Create project. Captions and basic edits work on the free plan, but AI features such as AI Edit, eye contact and caption styles need a paid plan to export.
site_article.hero_alt: A woman with long dark hair in a white top next to an AI twin progress overlay on a light blue background.

paragraphs.text: Captions is an AI video editor built by Mirage, a New York AI research company, and it runs on iPhone, Android and the web at captions.ai, according to its help center. If you want to know how to use Captions AI, the short version: record or import a talking video, let AI Edit cut it, check the captions, then export. Basic editing is free. The AI parts are not.

Captions works best for one person talking to the camera. Its own docs recommend a single speaker, say captions work best on clips of 60 to 90 seconds, and suggest keeping imported footage under three minutes for AI Edit.
How to use Captions AI Edit on your phone

paragraphs.title: 1. Update the app
paragraphs.text: AI Edit is rolling out on iOS, according to the help center. If you do not see it, update the app first.

paragraphs.title: 2. Start an Edit project
paragraphs.text: On the Home screen, keep Edit selected and add your media. Pick a style, such as Cozy, Vox-Style or Tour, and if you want, type a short description of the edit you have in mind. Tap Continue.

paragraphs.title: 3. Choose the options
paragraphs.text: Pick a model, then review Inputs and options: the aspect ratio, a Voiceover only toggle, and the output shape, Portrait 9:16 or Landscape 16:9. Set the effort level: Quick is the default, then Standard, Advanced and Ultra. Ultra puts the result ahead of speed and cost.

paragraphs.title: 4. Check the credit estimate and create
paragraphs.text: Before you start, Captions shows an estimated range of credits. The help center says you never pay more than the top of that range, and shows the real usage after each result. Tap Create project.
Decide on the model and effort before you tap Create project. The docs say you cannot change the model after a project starts, or the effort after it is created.

paragraphs.title: 5. Fix things by hand when you can
paragraphs.text: Manual edits on the timeline use no credits. Follow up edits you ask for in the chat do use credits, so small trims are cheaper to make yourself.
Add captions and translations

To caption a video on iPhone, import or record it, choose the spoken language, then choose No Translation or a target language, according to the help center. The help page lists about 100 languages, plus a Multiple Languages option. You can also add a caption by hand: tap Add, type it, then Apply.

There are length limits. Same language captions work on videos up to 10 minutes on iOS and the web and 5 minutes on Android. Captions in another language and dubbing are limited to 5 minutes on every platform. On the web, the help center says changing the caption style costs extra credits.
Dubbing, eye contact and AI Twin

Dubbing replaces the audio with another language, and Lipdub also re-animates the speaker's lips, according to Captions. It lists more than 30 dubbing languages, including Spanish, French, German, Hindi, Japanese and Portuguese, and says Lipdub clones your voice. Captions says you can start dubbing for free, while Lipdub is a premium feature.

Eye Contact is a tool in the app's editing panel that corrects your gaze after recording, for talking head footage. AI Twin creates an avatar of you from a short recording where you read a script; Captions lists it as a Max plan feature and recommends recording in a quiet room.
Captions AI plans and credits

The free plan includes basic tools such as trim, transitions, zoom and sound effects, one caption template and no AI credits, according to the pricing page. Max costs $24.99 a month with 500 credits. Frontier costs $69.99 a month with 1,400 credits, and Frontier 2x and 4x cost $139.99 and $279.99 for 2,800 and 5,600 credits. Captions says these prices reflect its iOS plans. An independent review by eesel AI lists the same prices and credit amounts.

Unused credits roll over to the next month, up to three times your monthly allowance, according to the credits page. Individual top ups are not available on standard plans, and canceling forfeits the remaining credits at the end of the period.

paragraphs.title: 6. Export
paragraphs.text: Tap Export, choose your settings and tap Export again. Advanced options include resolution, frame rate, bitrate and a separate SRT caption file. Basic manual edits export free, but the help center says AI features such as AI Edit, caption styles, eye contact correction and background music need a paid subscription, and the app asks for one when you export.
What Captions is bad at
Try your edit on the free plan before you pay. You only find out at export that a feature you used needs a subscription, so it is worth knowing which tools are AI features first.

Captions is built for short videos of one person talking. The help center itself steers you toward clips of a minute or two, and the five minute caps on translation and dubbing rule it out for long interviews. The eesel AI review also points to a learning curve and to app store complaints about lag, captions going out of sync after edits and crashes at export. Credits make the monthly cost hard to predict if you lean on chat edits and high effort levels, so start with Quick and do small fixes by hand.
